shots.title: Parse the invocation into discrete commands and match the flag only when it is an argument of gh pr merge (#683)

hazards.description: [code review] Guard used find() and inspected only the first gh pr merge, so a stacked-PR set whose last merge carries the delete flag fell through. Regression against the pre-existing regex.

shots.notes: New src/cli/guards/command-parse.ts segments a Bash invocation into commands and argv tokens, tracking each token's byte span. commandMatches() requires the program and subcommand words to be unquoted, so `echo "gh pr merge"` never matches. Leading env assignments are skipped so `GH_TOKEN=x gh pr merge` still resolves.

shots.title: Exclude heredoc bodies and quoted string literals from guard command matching (#683)

hazards.description: First cut mis-parsed the `<<<` herestring: the leading `<` fell through to a token, then the second and third `<` matched the two-character heredoc test, so the herestring's argument was consumed as a heredoc delimiter and the rest of the command vanished. Fixed by counting the full `<` run before deciding. Caught by a test written for the case, not by review.

[code review] Heredoc terminator was trimmed, so an indented body line closed the heredoc and put the document back into the token stream, reproducing the exact #683 false positive with the guard rewrite editing the document body. Found by independent code review.

[code review] CRLF heredoc opener yielded a delimiter with a trailing carriage return, which no body line matched, so the parser swallowed the rest of the command and every converted guard silently stopped protecting. This repo runs on Windows.

shots.notes: The scanner honours single quotes, double quotes with backslash escapes, line continuations, and heredoc bodies (quoted, unquoted and `<<-` tab-stripped delimiters). A heredoc body is skipped entirely rather than tokenized, so documentation *about* a flag can never read as passing it. An unterminated heredoc hands the remainder back to the tokenizer — a deliberate divergence from the shell, since discarding it makes guards fail open.

shots.title: Anchor the -d short flag to an argument position and make the suggested rewrite byte-identical apart from the removed flag (#683)

hazards.description: The `--flag=value` head split has to be restricted to long flags. Applying it to short flags re-created the original bug from the other direction: `cut -d=` splits to `-d` and matches. Short flags take their value adjacently, long flags take it after `=`.

shots.notes: findFlagToken matches whole tokens (or a `--flag=value` head), skips quoted tokens, and stops at a bare `--`. removeToken splices the token plus its preceding whitespace out of the ORIGINAL string, so the suggestion differs from what the operator typed only by the flag — the previous non-global regex replace rewrote the first match anywhere, including inside prose being written to a file.

shots.title: Audit the remaining Bash PreToolUse guards for the same raw-substring match and fix any that share it (#683)

hazards.description: version-check was the worst of the remaining set and was not in the issue: `command.includes('git push')` AND `/(main|master)/` over the raw text, gating a deny. Any command mentioning both strings — a release note, an issue body, a heredoc — was blocked from running. It also fired on a branch merely containing 'main', e.g. feat/maintenance.

[architect review] The guard audit was declared complete while sprint-completion still matched gh pr merge and slope validate by raw regex, and that guard WRITES sprint state. A heredoc body advanced the sprint phase from document prose. The audit grepped for one accessor and missed a guard reading the command another way.

[architect review] Three copies of a heredoc-blind shell tokenizer remained in the same directory as the new parser, in phase-boundary, sprint-completion and worktree-check. Duplication was not consolidated until review flagged it.

[code review] Test-runner detection stayed on a raw regex while four sibling detections were converted, so filing an issue whose body mentioned vitest set the tests gate, which gates PR creation. Contradicted the fix commit stated invariant.

shots.notes: First pass converted the four guards that deny on a raw-text match: version-check, worktree-self-remove, worktree-merge, branch-before-commit. That pass was scoped by grepping for tool_input.command, which missed sprint-completion — it reads the command another way and WRITES state. Independent review found it, and the audit was completed only afterwards: sprint-completion, phase-boundary and worktree-check all moved onto shellCommandSegments and their three private tokenizer copies were deleted. pr-review, post-push and push-nudge are advisory; shell-write matches raw text by design, since detecting heredocs and inline interpreters is its whole purpose. Lesson: audit by behaviour (which guards act on command text) not by accessor name.

bunker_locations: Any guard matching a flag or phrase against the raw Bash invocation will fire on commands that merely carry the text as data — issue bodies, commit messages, heredocs writing documentation. Parse to argv tokens instead; src/cli/guards/command-parse.ts exists for this.

A guard that rewrites the command it blocks must splice the original string by byte span. A regex replace over raw text edits the first match anywhere, so following the guard's own advice can silently corrupt file content.
notes: Fixes #683. The reported guard blocked the filing of its own bug report twice and mangled `cut -d= -f2-` into `cut= -f2-` in its suggested fix. Root cause was three defects in ten lines: an unanchored `-d\b` alternative, both regexes testing the whole invocation, and a non-global replace producing the suggestion. Scored triple_plus rather than par: three independent review passes (architect, code, verification) found six defects in this sprint's own code, two critical — a state-writing guard left on raw-text matching, and a tests gate an issue body could satisfy. The two self-authored review passes that preceded them caught none of it. The score reflects what independent review found, not what the implementer believed. All fixed and re-verified; suite 4346 passing.
